rule: PAP-077-2 (standing from v0.77). No question may exist twice in the bank. An official past paper beats a PMT question, the earlier PMT question beats a later one, and a second copy of the same official paper is skipped. scripts/duplicates.py lists candidates; an agent confirms each by looking at both questions and records it here. scripts/luisa.py check (the gate) fails on any candidate not recorded here, any duplicateOf link, and any removed ID still in the bank.

thresholds.note: A pair involving an official or PMT question is a candidate from similarity 0.4; a pair of Luisa or Practice Booklet questions from 0.95.

notDuplicates.why: Same wording, different diagram: A and B are at different intersections (q17.png against q21.png, viewed).
Stretch parallel to the y-axis against the x-axis; a different exercise on the same function list.
Reflection in the x-axis against the y-axis; a different exercise on the same function list.
Different roots (1+i, -2, 3 against -1+2i and 3-i) and no Argand diagram part.
Different problem: the PMT question gives a square of roots with z1 = 2+3i.
Different roots (2+i and 4-3i) and no Argand diagram part.
Derivative of cos (June 2018) against derivative of sin (Sample); different questions.
Different curves (y = x^2 - 2x - 24 sqrt x against y = 3x^4 - 8x^3 - 3) with the same part structure.
Different cubic (x^3+3x^2-8x+6 against x^3-7x^2-12x+6) and transformation (alpha-1 against alpha+2).
Different expression ((1-cos 2theta)/(3theta sin 2theta) against (1-cos 4theta)/(2theta sin 3theta)).
Different series (1/((2r-1)(2r+1)) against 1/((r+1)(r+2))).
Different cubic and transformation (2alpha+1 against alpha-1).
v0.76 decision: different equation (64cosh^4 x - 64cosh^2 x - 9 = 0 against sinh 2x = 3 sinh x); only the boilerplate instruction lines are shared.
Different requested probability representations (Venn versus tree), events and part marks.
Different small-angle inputs and numerical approximations.
Different given height, unknown and numerical force data.
Different function domains and order of composition.
Different functions to differentiate from first principles.
Different regression data and measured quantities.
Different rational expressions and integral.
Fourth versus sixth power in the binomial expansion.
Different quadratic and line and therefore a different bounded area.
Different parabola and line.
Different paired observations and context.
Different masses, incline and initial motion.
Fourth power versus square in the limit definition.
Different position and displacement vectors.
Different ladder angle, weight and requested unknown.
Volume change versus surface-area change.
Different masses, angles and friction conditions.
Different rational functions and transformed values.
Different trigonometric functions and bounds.
Different velocity vectors and requested speed or bearing.
Different body, force, angle and setup.
Different trajectory angles and requested flight time or distance.
Different measured variables and numerical datasets.
Different cubic polynomials and factorisations.
Different curve and line equations and intersection points.
Different probabilities, events and unknowns.
Different sample size and hypothesised proportion.
Different mass, incline and rope conditions.
Different induction identities. The official summand has denominator (2r−1)(2r+1); the Luisa summand has denominator (r+1)(r+2).
Both describe motion along a straight line. The 2025 paper gives displacement 2t³−12t²+18t and asks for maximum speed in part (c). The 2022 paper gives t³/3−5t²/2+6t and has two parts.
The sample transforms roots by subtracting 1 from each. The 2018 paper transforms a different cubic by doubling each root and adding 1.
Only the divisibility statement in the second part recurs. AS Q7 also requires a separate five-mark proof of the reciprocal sum; the official six-mark A-level Q6 asks only for divisibility.
The AS question specifically requires induction. The textbook starts with a fourth-power difference identity and specifically requires the method of differences. Only the final sum of cubes agrees.
The official second assertion adds 3 before squaring. The booklet adds 2.
The booklet differentiates 3x squared; the official prompt differentiates x cubed.
Sample Q6 differentiates 3x squared. June 2018 Q10 differentiates x cubed.
The two questions use different position vectors and have different displacements and magnitudes.
The official estimate is for 1.995 to the seventh power. The booklet asks for 1.985 to the seventh power, requiring a different substitution.
